main_text.p: absolvit & justos pronunciat. Unde etiam à mor-te, quæ peccato sublato necessario aboletur, nos liberatos esse constat, licet animę & corporis dis-solutionem adhuc patiamur, non ut moriamur, sed ut in vitam sempiternam transferamur, quę beneficia tam morti quam resurrectioni tribuū-tur, quoniam illa parta, hac confirmantur & con-feruntur. Accedit his tertius fructus, quod virtute mortis ac resurrectionis Christi natura nostra in-3. Instauratio naturæ propter S.S.stauratur, & nos toti ad novam vitā regeneramur per Spiritum sanctum: quod beneficium paucis quidem verbis indicat propheta noster, cum ait: nos livore eius sanatos esse: Apostolus vero ad Rom. 4. Resurrectio & glorificatio ecclesiæ6. illustrius exponit. Gloriosam denique, corporum ex morte suscitationem, propter Christi resurrec-tionem credimus & speramus. Nisi n. ipsi quoq; ad vitam beatè in omnem æternitatem degēdam excitaremur, irrita fieret Iesaię promissio, quādo visurum Messiam semē, & habituū generationē æt. pollicetur, propterea q; ipse caput nostri ū cum sit, nobis membris suis carere non poterat. Ac valde illustris est Pauli illa inter Adamū & Christum 1 Cor. 15.oppositio, quando perinde in Christo vivificari oēs nos oportere demonstrat, atq; in Adamo oēs sumus mortui. Verū, auditores, sentio me copia argumenti hujus ita obrui, ut quasi in vastum pelagus abreptus, quo me expediam modo, aut quo modo paucis multa, nedum oīa dicam, nō videā[?]. Superant sanè beneficia Christi omnem humanā [illegible, ~8 letters]eloquentiam, & video hic ante oculos abyssum magnam omnigenæ consolationis: quoniam omnia, quæ CHRISTUS fecit, saluti nostræ
[Remainder of the final line is partly covered by the margin note; no further printed text.]

page.notes: The margin note numbered 3 reads "Instauratio naturæ propter S.S." and note 4 reads "Resurrectio & glorificatio ecclesiæ"; the words after "pro-" and "glorifica-" are cramped at the outer edge. The Greek marginal note beside "humanā" is too faint to read and is marked illegible. The final line's ending is partly obscured by a margin note and the page edge; "nostræ" is a reading from a fragment. The catchword "servire" is read from a partly faded print and may be "seruire" in the original. The word "videā" is doubtful. The right edge of the page is damaged and there is show-through from the page behind.
